entries.description: Giant House-point hourglasses occupy wall niches in an Entrance Hall corner. Gems rise from the lower bulbs as points are deducted; Slytherin’s contains emeralds. The marble staircase reaches the same hall.
entries.temporal: Early April 1996; Pensieve scenes in Snape’s fifth-year O.W.L. summer where specified
entries.model_notes: Specific gem only given for Slytherin here; Gryffindor is later nearly empty.

entries.description: Fred and George say they forced Montague headfirst into a Vanishing Cabinet on the first floor and do not know where he went. Later Malfoy reports him jammed in a fourth-floor toilet, confused.
entries.temporal: Early April 1996; Pensieve scenes in Snape’s fifth-year O.W.L. summer where specified
entries.model_notes: Both incident accounts are reported. Do not infer an ordinary passage linking those floors.

entries.description: Filch takes Harry from the Entrance Hall up the marble staircase past its first landing to Umbridge’s office.
entries.temporal: Early April 1996; Pensieve scenes in Snape’s fifth-year O.W.L. summer where specified
entries.model_notes: Third-floor location established elsewhere; this journey omits intervening details.

entries.description: A large wooden HEADMISTRESS block with gold letters lies across the desk front. Harry’s Firebolt and the twins’ Cleansweeps are chained and padlocked to a stout iron wall peg behind the desk; kitten plates animate overhead.
entries.temporal: Early April 1996; Pensieve scenes in Snape’s fifth-year O.W.L. summer where specified
entries.model_notes: Confiscated storage is now directly observed.

entries.description: Umbridge conjures drinks onto her desk and gives Harry tea in a cup and saucer. During the distraction he empties it into a nearby vase of dried flowers.
entries.temporal: Early April 1996; Pensieve scenes in Snape’s fifth-year O.W.L. summer where specified
entries.model_notes: Tea contamination not established here; cup does not prove a permanent refreshment station.

entries.description: Umbridge says every Hogwarts fire except her own is watched by a Floo Network Regulator, the Squad reads all owl post and Filch monitors all secret routes into and out of the castle.
entries.temporal: Early April 1996; Pensieve scenes in Snape’s fifth-year O.W.L. summer where specified
entries.model_notes: Reported surveillance scope and explicit office-fire exception; does not mean every passage is physically closed.

entries.location: Fireworks outbreak and route to second floor
entries.description: One floor below Umbridge’s office, fireworks fill corridors with green-and-gold dragons, five-foot pink Catherine wheels, silver-tailed rockets, airborne written words and firecrackers. A wheel exits a stair window across the grounds; dragons and a purple bat use an open corridor-end door toward the second floor.
entries.temporal: Early April 1996; Pensieve scenes in Snape’s fifth-year O.W.L. summer where specified
entries.model_notes: Narration says one floor down, then movement toward second floor; preserve both without forcing a geometrically consistent floor grid.

entries.description: A Stunned rocket explodes and blasts a hole in a painting of a witch in a meadow; she escapes into the adjacent card-playing wizards’ painting. Filch takes a broom from a nearby cupboard and its head catches fire.
entries.temporal: Early April 1996; Pensieve scenes in Snape’s fifth-year O.W.L. summer where specified
entries.model_notes: Specific local damage and neighbouring frames; no restoration shown.

entries.description: Harry ducks through a door concealed behind a tapestry a short way along the fireworks corridor, finding the twins just behind it.
entries.temporal: Early April 1996; Pensieve scenes in Snape’s fifth-year O.W.L. summer where specified
entries.model_notes: Unnamed hidden opening; no destination beyond this refuge supplied.

entries.description: Fireworks continue spreading into classrooms all afternoon; George says Vanishing them multiplies them tenfold. Escaped rockets pass Gryffindor windows at night; a Catherine-wheel/rocket collision produces flying pink-and-silver piglets.
entries.temporal: Early April 1996; Pensieve scenes in Snape’s fifth-year O.W.L. summer where specified
entries.model_notes: Multiplication is reported; persistence, outdoor flights and hybrid display observed. Lower Gryffindor dormitories are audible beneath Harry’s.

entries.description: After the interrupted lesson the Pensieve stands on Snape’s desk, casting rippling silvery light onto the wall and doorframe. Harry views the Hall memory through its transparent contents, then enters it.
entries.temporal: Early April 1996; Pensieve scenes in Snape’s fifth-year O.W.L. summer where specified
entries.model_notes: Memory-space access is magical, not a physical opening in the desk or school floor.

entries.description: In Snape’s O.W.L. memory the four House tables are absent, replaced by over a hundred small tables facing one direction, with aisles for invigilation. Sunlight enters through high windows.
entries.temporal: Early April 1996; Pensieve scenes in Snape’s fifth-year O.W.L. summer where specified
entries.model_notes: Narrated Pensieve observation of past layout, not present-day furniture.

entries.description: The exam crowd leaves through doors into the Entrance Hall and front doors to sunlit grounds, then walks down the lawn toward the lake.
entries.temporal: Early April 1996; Pensieve scenes in Snape’s fifth-year O.W.L. summer where specified
entries.model_notes: Travel shown in Snape’s memory; no invented date beyond his O.W.L. year.

entries.description: James’s group sits on grass beneath the same lakeside beech used by Harry’s group in autumn. Nearby dense bushes shade Snape; girls sit on the bank with bare feet in the smooth sunlit water. Open grass between them accommodates the confrontation.
entries.temporal: Early April 1996; Pensieve scenes in Snape’s fifth-year O.W.L. summer where specified
entries.model_notes: Explicit cross-time identity of beech. Short wand-flight distances are action positions, not a fixed site plan.

entries.location: Snape study stone floor and jar damage
entries.description: Harry returns from the Pensieve to the study’s stone floor. Snape throws him down; a jar of dead cockroaches explodes over his head as he exits. Harry flees along the corridor and climbs until three floors separate them.
entries.temporal: Early April 1996; Pensieve scenes in Snape’s fifth-year O.W.L. summer where specified
entries.model_notes: Local breakage and flight; stopping floor is not named and no repair is shown.

entries.description: Easter grows brighter, breezier and warmer while exam years remain inside studying.
entries.temporal: Easter and start of summer term, April 1996
entries.model_notes: Seasonal transition; not a claimed lake temperature.

entries.description: Pince stamps books several shelves away from the table. Discovering Harry and Ginny eating chocolate, she enchants his books, bag and ink bottle to chase and strike them out of the library.
entries.temporal: Easter and start of summer term, April 1996
entries.model_notes: Observed enforcement enchantment; no permanent self-attacking furniture.

entries.description: Careers pamphlets and leaflets appear on common-room tables, and the noticeboard lists fifth-year appointments with the Head of House.
entries.temporal: Easter and start of summer term, April 1996
entries.model_notes: Holiday-to-summer-term information state.

entries.description: The twins plan a five-o’clock diversion in the east wing, in Gregory the Smarmy’s corridor, intending to draw Umbridge away from her office.
entries.temporal: Easter and start of summer term, April 1996
entries.model_notes: Planned location, later swamp corroborates east-wing area. Do not place Umbridge’s office in a particular opposite wing.

entries.description: From the window beside Neville’s bed Harry looks directly toward the towering lakeside beech. He also sees Hagrid emerge limping from the Forest edge, enter his cabin and send smoke from its chimney.
entries.temporal: Easter and start of summer term, April 1996
entries.model_notes: Critical dormitory-to-beech, Forest and cabin sightlines; no azimuths or exact distances.

entries.description: Harry places an Invigoration Draught sample at Snape’s desk; it is smashed on the floor after he turns away. Hermione has already emptied his remaining cauldron.
entries.temporal: Easter and start of summer term, April 1996
entries.model_notes: Observed broken sample, cause not directly witnessed; no structural damage.

entries.description: Harry leaves Divination and hurries back upstairs for careers advice in McGonagall’s office. Her desk is covered in pamphlets; Umbridge sits in a corner behind Harry, and their argument remains audible along the corridor as he leaves.
entries.temporal: Easter and start of summer term, April 1996
entries.model_notes: Ground-floor Divination now in classroom eleven; no numerical office floor derived.

entries.description: After Defence Harry hears uproar above; Umbridge runs in the opposite direction toward the east wing. In the deserted corridor to her office he hides behind a large suit of armour whose helmet turns to watch him.
entries.temporal: Easter and start of summer term, April 1996
entries.model_notes: Animated armour and usable hiding space; not an exact distance or floor count.

entries.location: Umbridge office lock and Floo hearth
entries.description: Sirius’s magical knife opens the office door with a click. A small Floo-powder box sits by the empty grate, with stacked logs; powder ignites emerald flames. Harry kneels on a hard stone floor and sends only his head to Grimmauld Place, withdrawing it as the flames die.
entries.temporal: Easter and start of summer term, April 1996
entries.model_notes: Successful lock bypass observed; immunity to Alohomora was only Harry’s earlier guess.

entries.location: Office desk drawer and stair return
entries.description: Filch enters the unlocked office and searches a desk drawer for a form. Harry follows him, removes his Cloak one landing below the office and descends the marble staircase to the Entrance Hall.
entries.temporal: Easter and start of summer term, April 1996
entries.model_notes: No assumption the first landing down is the only intermediate floor.

entries.description: In the Entrance Hall Umbridge accuses the twins of turning a school corridor into a swamp; Fred advertises a Portable Swamp demonstrated upstairs. Some assembled pupils are covered in a Stinksap-like substance.
entries.temporal: Easter and start of summer term, April 1996
entries.model_notes: Swamp existence stated by participants; precise extent is described next chapter. Stinksap identity is Harry’s comparison.

entries.location: Broom retrieval and Entrance Hall escape
entries.description: Summoned brooms rip free with a distant crash and fly along a corridor to Harry’s left, turn left down the stairs and stop by the twins; one trails its heavy chain and iron peg over the flagged floor. They rise fifteen feet in the Hall and fly through open front doors into sunset.
entries.temporal: Easter and start of summer term, April 1996
entries.model_notes: Demonstrates vertical clearance and chained peg removal; Harry’s own broom is not retrieved in this scene.

entries.description: The swamp fills a fifth-floor east-wing corridor. After failed removal attempts the area is roped off, and Filch punts pupils across to their classrooms.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Essential temporary route obstruction and boat transport; teachers’ ability to remove it is Harry’s belief, not a demonstrated limitation.

entries.location: Umbridge door replaced and broom moved
entries.description: Two broom-shaped holes remain in Umbridge’s office door until Filch replaces it. He moves Harry’s Firebolt to the dungeons; an armed security troll guarding it is rumoured.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Door replacement and broom relocation narrated; troll specifically unconfirmed.

entries.description: A Niffler tears Umbridge’s office apart seeking shiny objects and tries biting her rings. Frequent Dungbombs and Stink Pellets prompt pupils to wear Bubble-Head Charms for fresh air in corridors.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Damage extent unspecified; do not model permanent poisonous corridors.

entries.description: Peeves overturns tables, bursts through blackboards, topples statues and vases, smashes lanterns, extinguishes candles, juggles burning torches, throws papers into fires or out of windows, traps Mrs Norris twice inside armour, and drops tarantulas into the Great Hall at breakfast.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Series of narrated local incidents; not evidence every object of these classes is destroyed.

entries.description: Peeves pulls all taps from the second-floor bathrooms and floods that floor. A week after the twins leave Harry sees him loosening a crystal chandelier.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Bathroom floor explicit; chandelier floor unspecified, and complete fall not narrated.

entries.description: From the Charms classroom window Hermione watches Montague’s parents stride up the front drive and enter the castle.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Classroom-to-drive/front-entry sightline, no orientation or floor.

entries.description: Pupils animate teacups on desks with legs, including willow-pattern legs; one cup breaks and is repaired, another walks over the desk edge and smashes on the floor.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Lesson props and local breakage, not persistent moving furniture.

entries.description: Harry and Hermione sit in the second-highest row; Hagrid reaches them along the row behind, then they edge along their seats to stairs down to the lawn. From the stand edge he checks the lawn to his cabin, and they cross it toward the Forest.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Hagrid uses crowded spectator circulation; no width measurement.

entries.description: At the cabin Hermione turns left toward its front door; Hagrid continues straight to the outermost trees and picks up a crossbow leaning against a tree before entering the Forest.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Left is relative to this stadium approach; weapon is a temporary stored prop.

entries.description: They follow an increasingly overgrown path through protruding roots, low branches and dense dusk-like shade, passing far beyond the Thestral clearing. Hagrid then leaves the path toward the Forest heart through knotted brambles and thorn thickets that delay the pupils.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: No creatures encountered initially; cause only later inferred by Harry.

entries.description: After a pause they continue another fifteen minutes past nettles and arrive behind a barricade of uprooted trunks and branches on a bare patch of ground.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Fifteen minutes starts after the conversation pause, not at the original Forest edge.

entries.description: Grawp sleeps curled on bare earth amid uprooted trees. His curved back initially resembles a mound nearly Hagrid’s height and his head a mossy boulder to its left. The surrounding trunks and boughs form a fence-like barrier.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Descriptions are initial visual comparisons, not actual earth mound or constructed stone shelter.

entries.description: Thick ropes like saplings bind Grawp’s wrists and ankles to the largest nearby tree trunks. He is at least sixteen feet tall, with sledge-sized bare feet, a huge round head, animal-skin smock and umbrella-sized hands; the anchor trees creak when he stands.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Initial height reported by Hagrid and subsequently confirmed by narrator; allow rope tension and reach in the model.

entries.description: Hagrid says Grawp feeds himself on birds and deer. Grawp takes a nest from a towering pine, drops its eggs, bends the treetop until the roots crack, and eventually pulls the pine over; pupils hide behind a trunk to avoid his grasp.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Feeding range reported; nest destruction, tree bending and distant crash narrated. Keep this local damage temporal.

entries.description: Returning through thick knotgrass, they encounter Magorian and four or five other armed centaurs. The herd bars Hagrid after his rescue of Firenze, but permits passage because children are present, claiming not to harm foals; it warns about his concealed giant.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Reported territorial rules alongside observed confrontation; no guaranteed safety for every student encounter.

entries.description: They skirt the same nettles, rejoin the path and walk another ten minutes until trees thin, sky appears, and the stadium is visible from the Forest shelter. They merge with matchgoers returning uphill to the castle.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Ten minutes begins after rejoining path; stadium/Forest reciprocal sightline explicit.

entries.location: Front entrance lintel and Forest view
entries.description: Celebrants carrying Ron bump his head on the castle doorway lintel while squeezing into the Entrance Hall. Harry and Hermione climb the steps and look back from the front doors toward distant Forest treetops, where Harry thinks birds erupt upward.
entries.temporal: May 1996, post-twins unrest and final Quidditch match
entries.model_notes: Lintel impact confirms finite doorway clearance; birds and uprooting explanation remain tentative.

entries.description: The friends again revise in the lakeside beech’s shade, near other pupils. In June the cloudless sky reflects in a smooth sparkling lake and satin-green lawns ripple in a light breeze.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: Warm late-May/June state; lake clearly liquid again.

entries.description: Hermione describes Grawp as sixteen feet tall and the pines he uproots as twenty feet tall.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: Reported approximate pine height, supplementary to direct Forest observations.

entries.description: Sprout admits the queued students into greenhouse three for Herbology revision.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: Specific classroom identity, without additional inferred contents.

entries.location: Entrance Hall and Great Hall sightline
entries.description: From dinner seats pupils can see the examiners through the Great Hall’s double doors into the Entrance Hall; they cross the threshold and linger at the marble stair foot.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: Line of sight from dining space to Hall circulation; broom-cupboard emergence is only a simile about Marchbanks’s search.

entries.description: After breakfast the House tables are replaced with individual tables facing the staff-table end. A desk by the presiding teacher holds an enormous hourglass, spare quills, ink and parchment. House tables return at lunchtime.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: Daily furniture conversion and stone floor confirmed; sunlight heats desks and reaches Harry’s head.

entries.description: Pupils wait in the small chamber beside the Great Hall, entering the Hall in alphabetical groups; tested pupils do not return. Flitwick stands just inside the door and directs Harry to an examiner’s small table in a far corner.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: Waiting room adjacency and one-way exam circulation, without a fixed room name.

entries.description: Exam props include a levitated wineglass that smashes, an egg cup, rat, dinner plate and Transfiguration animals; a ferret becomes flamingos requiring temporary evacuation. Defence practice includes Boggart banishing, and Harry’s stag Patronus canters the Hall’s length.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: Transient practical testing materials; no claim all exam subjects use identical station layouts.

entries.description: At an open common-room window Harry and Ron play chess in warm air while watching Hagrid teach at the Forest edge; Harry guesses unicorns from the boys standing back.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: Hagrid and class observed; unicorn identification remains a guess. Hermione reports another Niffler attack in Umbridge’s office.

entries.description: The creature practical takes place on the lawn at the Forest edge, with a Knarl among a dozen hedgehogs, milk, Bowtruckle handling, a Fire Crab to feed and clean, and food choices for a sick unicorn. Hagrid watches from his cabin window.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: Exam materials confirmed; a real sick unicorn is not explicitly present. Cabin-to-exam-lawn sightline.

entries.description: Harry’s practical uses a desktop, blank crystal ball, tea-leaf reading and an examiner’s palm; afterward the friends ascend the marble staircase.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: No specific exam-room identity supplied beyond ascent afterward.

entries.description: At eleven the pupils set telescopes on stands at the top of the Astronomy Tower beside a parapet, writing star charts while examiners circulate. They later descend a spiral staircase to its foot.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: Open sky observing area with parapet; telescope holders also used. No roof or dome invented.

entries.description: Harry stands at a parapet directly above the castle front doors. When they open, light spills down the stone steps onto the lawn; he can see people crossing it, castle-window lights reflected on the ground and the cabin’s lit windows and door.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: Strong vertical alignment and multi-point sightlines; no total tower height stated.

entries.description: Six attackers enter Hagrid’s lit cabin, then its door bursts open into a fight outside. Fang is Stunned, one attacker thrown about ten feet and others knocked down. McGonagall is struck by four Stunners halfway between cabin and castle.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: Observed from distant tower; thrown distance is Harry’s estimate. Hagrid’s spell resistance is observed, cause later attributed to giant ancestry.

entries.description: Hagrid lifts unconscious Fang around his shoulders and runs toward the distant gates, vanishing into darkness under a missed final Stunning Spell.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: Direction and disappearance observed; destination with Dumbledore only conjectured.

entries.description: Lee admits he put the Nifflers in Umbridge’s office by levitating them through her window.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: Reported exterior-window access, explaining entry despite the new door.

entries.description: Colin says pupils watched through a dormitory window as McGonagall was carried back uphill to the castle.
entries.temporal: Late May–June 1996 O.W.L. examinations and night raid
entries.model_notes: Reported view from Colin’s dormitory, not necessarily Harry’s window or room.

entries.location: Hall to hospital wing and first floor
entries.description: Harry exits the exam to the Entrance Hall, climbs the marble staircase and further flights through portrait-lined corridors, entering the hospital wing through double doors. Returning, he descends two floors to the marble staircase top and follows the first-floor corridor.
entries.temporal: June 1996, immediately after final History of Magic exam
entries.model_notes: Text supplies a two-floor descent and first-floor endpoint; retain those constraints without forcing an absolute hospital floor in this entry.

entries.description: Pomfrey treats Montague inside the wing; a bell rings immediately outside the dormitory/ward as students move through corridors above and below.
entries.temporal: June 1996, immediately after final History of Magic exam
entries.model_notes: McGonagall has been transferred to St Mungo’s; do not conflate the external hospital with this wing.

entries.description: Harry peers into doorways along the first-floor corridor, selects an empty classroom and shuts its door. He sits on a desk; Hermione later paces between desks. His shouts are audible to Ginny and Luna outside.
entries.temporal: June 1996, immediately after final History of Magic exam
entries.model_notes: Distinct unnamed usable classroom with desks and a door; no furnishings borrowed from other lessons.

entries.description: Ron proposes sending Umbridge to the Transfiguration department, which he describes as far from her office. Lookouts redirect traffic around the office corridor by the swivelling staircase.
entries.temporal: June 1996, immediately after final History of Magic exam
entries.model_notes: Transfiguration distance is Ron’s qualitative report. Gas is a fabricated cover story, not an actual hazard.

entries.description: From the empty classroom Harry goes up, meets Dean and Seamus two floors higher, then retrieves the Cloak and knife through Gryffindor’s portrait hole; a few minutes later he descends the last stairs to the office corridor.
entries.temporal: June 1996, immediately after final History of Magic exam
entries.model_notes: Do not equate the meeting floor with the portrait-hole floor unless independently stated.

entries.description: A recess contains an ugly stone head of a medieval wizard on a column, muttering in Latin; Harry and Hermione conceal themselves behind it to don the Cloak.
entries.temporal: June 1996, immediately after final History of Magic exam
entries.model_notes: Stone talking bust and hiding recess, distinct from Paracelsus unless future evidence identifies it.

entries.description: The magical knife again opens the lock. Late-afternoon sunshine warms the animated kitten plates. Hermione watches the grounds from the window, staying out of sight, while Harry uses Floo powder at the hearth.
entries.temporal: June 1996, immediately after final History of Magic exam
entries.model_notes: Observed window-to-grounds view; no compass bearing.

entries.description: Umbridge catches Harry at the fireplace and says Stealth Sensoring Spells surround her doorway, installed after the last Niffler. She says the Firebolt is strictly guarded in the dungeons.
entries.temporal: June 1996, immediately after final History of Magic exam
entries.model_notes: Detection implementation and broom guarding reported by Umbridge; confirms neither a specific troll nor impermeability of the door.

entries.description: The office contains a chintz-covered armchair and a carpet; Ron’s bleeding lip stains it. Malfoy sits or leans on the windowsill while captors pin Hermione against a wall.
entries.temporal: June 1996, immediately after final History of Magic exam
entries.model_notes: Temporary crowded custody arrangement; dimensions not inferred from headcount.

entries.description: Umbridge says Filch has just reported Peeves smearing ink on all school telescope eyepieces.
entries.temporal: June 1996, immediately after final History of Magic exam
entries.model_notes: Reported sabotage; not confirmation of destruction or of the proposed Transfiguration rampage.

entries.description: Hermione leads from Umbridge’s corridor down stairs to the Entrance Hall, within about twenty feet of dinner through the Hall doors, then through oak front doors and down stone steps across the grass toward the Forest. The setting sun approaches the treetops ahead while shadows stretch behind them.
entries.temporal: June 1996 evening following final exam
entries.model_notes: Observed sun/view relation; no exact date-based azimuth inferred.

entries.description: Hermione takes a different path from the Grawp visit: Harry recognises the path used three years earlier toward Aragog’s lair. Brambles, a fallen sapling and thick undergrowth obstruct it; eventually the dense canopy blocks all light.
entries.temporal: June 1996 evening following final exam
entries.model_notes: Destination recognition is Harry’s memory; this group does not reach Aragog.

entries.description: They emerge into a dim damp clearing; an arrow strikes a tree above Hermione and roughly fifty armed centaurs encircle them. The group backs to the centre while hooves shake the floor and voices echo.
entries.temporal: June 1996 evening following final exam
entries.model_notes: Distinct clearing from Grawp’s tether site; Umbridge’s broken wand remains on the ground, and she is carried away through trees.

entries.description: Umbridge claims the Ministry permits centaurs only certain land; centaurs claim the Forest, reject wizard law and debate whether adolescents count as protected foals. They hold Harry and Hermione after she admits hoping to use them against Umbridge.
entries.temporal: June 1996 evening following final exam
entries.model_notes: Conflicting character claims, not a verified legal cadastral boundary.

entries.description: Grawp parts two thick trunks at the clearing edge, appearing under the branch canopy with broken ankle ropes trailing. Arrows strike his face; he scatters centaurs, then pursues them through the opposite trees, smashing trees aside.
entries.temporal: June 1996 evening following final exam
entries.model_notes: He has escaped restraints; no longer model him continuously tethered after this event.

entries.description: After sheltering among trees Harry kicks a nearby tree and a Bowtruckle chatters overhead, flexing long fingers. Ron’s group approaches through low branches.
entries.temporal: June 1996 evening following final exam
entries.model_notes: Actual Bowtruckle-in-tree habitat beyond the classroom specimens.

entries.description: Ron says the rescued pupils saw Harry and Hermione head into the Forest from Umbridge’s office window and followed after escaping their captors.
entries.temporal: June 1996 evening following final exam
entries.model_notes: Reported route and office-to-Forest sightline; exact tracking path unstated.

entries.description: Two Thestrals wait between trees; one licks Grawp’s blood from Harry’s sleeve. Another six or seven pick their way through the trees with wings tightly folded, providing mounts for six pupils.
entries.temporal: June 1996 evening following final exam
entries.model_notes: Blood attraction is Ginny’s inference, supported by licking and arrival; it is not an explicitly demonstrated summoning spell.

entries.description: Harry mounts from a nearby stump, securing his knees behind the wing joints; riders grip manes. Luna helps the three pupils unable to see the animals mount separate Thestrals.
entries.temporal: June 1996 sunset and night, Department of Mysteries expedition
entries.model_notes: Physical riding arrangement and stump aid, not saddles or bridles.

entries.description: On a spoken destination command, Thestrals extend their wings, crouch and climb steeply through the topmost branches into sunset. Six riders streak over the castle, grounds and Hogsmeade, then mountains, gullies, villages and winding hillside roads before reaching London after dark.
entries.temporal: June 1996 sunset and night, Department of Mysteries expedition
entries.model_notes: School boundary aerial egress and surrounding terrain; no speed, duration, exact bearing or continuous mapped road course supplied. London endpoint is Ministry visitors’ entrance.
